Raise the salary offer to $240,000 and reduce the equity. 

Your current bottleneck is cash competitiveness against large AI companies, not your interview process or founder time investment. At 3 weeks and 2 hours a week, your process is already efficient. 

Do not hire a recruiting agency; paying 25% for senior engineering hires during a cash crunch diverts capital from product velocity without solving the root wage deficit. Do not stop hiring to rely solely on coding agents; building a developer tool with only two engineers and two founders risks burnout and slows iteration when you need to capture market momentum post-seed. 

Adjusting the compensation mix to $240,000 cash while scaling back the 0.5% equity aligns your offer closer to market realities for senior backend talent while preserving startup upside. 

Material assumptions: your seed round of $3 million can support the higher burn rate for at least 18 to 24 months, and you can source qualified candidates willing to trade some prestige and cash for early-stage impact. 

Decision criteria: if your runway drops below 18 months at the $240,000 salary level, immediately revert to hiring one senior engineer combined with a strong contractor, or slow hiring until post-Series A traction justifies the increased burn.
